research_concepts: Brown->Tatum pick-and-roll premium (+0.326 points per chain as reported)
initiator-specific PNR effect versus any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR
derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) built from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Can the Brown-specific premium be distinguished from the any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR baseline with 43 Brown chains?
What chain count and per-chain variance are needed to detect a 0.326-point difference at useful power?
How reliable are play-type point values derived from play-by-play labels, and does the derivation rule match the study definition?
Do shot quality, defensive matchup, lineup, season, or playoff status confound the initiator comparison?
Is the comparison pre-specified, or was the +0.326 premium selected from many initiator and play-type contrasts?
evidence_establishes: No historical evidence was retrieved. The retrieve_history call returned an empty list (n_results: 0), so no prior study of this question, its data, or its methods is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the +0.326 Brown->Tatum premium is real, reproducible, or specific to Brown.
Whether any earlier analysis tested the initiator-specific versus any-teammate contrast.
How derived play-type point values behave in this data, or what variance they have.
Any power, reliability, or confounding result for this dataset.
own_inferences: The question is a contrast between one initiator and a pooled baseline. Its power depends on the number of baseline DRIVE->Tatum PNR chains, which the task does not report. With only 43 Brown chains, a chain-level standard error is likely large relative to 0.326 unless per-chain variance is small.
The +0.326 figure appears to come from a prior exploratory summary. Selecting the largest initiator-by-play-type contrast from many candidates would inflate its apparent size.
The data as of 2026-06-14 include the complete 2025-26 regular season but only partial 2025-26 playoffs, so playoff rows from that season must be excluded or handled as partial.
Shot distance and result, defensive matchup minutes, and lineup context are available, so the main confounders can be partly adjusted, but only if they are recorded at the chain level.
uncertainties: The number of any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR chains is not stated, so the baseline sample size is unknown.
Per-chain point variance and the standard error of the +0.326 estimate are not stated.
The exact derivation rule for play-type labels and points is not given, so label error is unquantified.
Whether the 43 Brown chains are one season or pooled across 2022-23 to 2025-26 is not stated.
Whether Tatum's role in each chain (screener versus roller) is recorded consistently is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no earlier result, failed approach, or prior analysis could alter the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the stated data constraints alone.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 43 Brown chains are available. A test of a 0.326-point difference against a pooled teammate baseline likely lacks power unless per-chain variance is small and the baseline is large. Neither is reported.
Brown-initiated DRIVE->Tatum PNR chains are sparse, and splitting them by season or playoff status would reduce cell sizes further.
Points per chain come from a derived play-type label built from play-by-play, so the outcome depends on the labeling rule rather than a directly recorded event.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No identifiers are cited.

risks.text: 43 Brown chains give a likely wide confidence interval around the premium. The test may be underpowered to separate Brown-specific from any-teammate effects.
The +0.326 premium was likely selected as a notable value from many initiator-by-play-type contrasts. Its magnitude is probably inflated, and regression toward the mean is expected on new data.
Comparing Brown against every teammate and every play type inflates the false-positive rate unless the contrast is pre-specified.
Shot quality, defender matchup (Tatum's and Brown's assigned defenders), lineup, and game context can drive points per chain independently of initiator identity.
Points per chain from play-by-play may be noisy because of sequence-attribution errors, and the reliability of the chain-level estimate is unknown.
The outcome is derived from play-type labels and points, so mislabeled DRIVE or PNR events propagate directly into the estimate.
Chain boundaries and the initiator attribution rule may be misassigned, which would move chains between the Brown and any-teammate groups.
The baseline any-teammate PNR points per chain is unknown, so the size of a 0.326 difference relative to the baseline cannot be judged.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 mixes rosters, coaching schemes, and playoff and regular-season contexts. The 2025-26 playoffs are partial as of 2026-06-14.
Splitting by season, playoff status, or defensive matchup leaves very small cells.

design.estimand: Difference in mean points per DRIVE->Tatum PNR chain between Brown-initiated and other-teammate-initiated chains, adjusted for shot quality, defender matchup, lineup, and season. Not to be run as posed until the baseline size and per-chain variance are reported.
design.unit: Chain: one DRIVE->Tatum PNR possession sequence, with initiator, play type, and points derived from play-by-play.
design.sample: Regular-season and playoff chains from 2022-23 to 2025-26, using only data complete as of 2026-06-14 (2025-26 regular season, complete from 2026-04-13; exclude 2025-26 playoff rows, which are partial). Minimum viable test: all teammate-initiated DRIVE->Tatum PNR chains, with Brown's 43 chains as the focal group.
design.power: Compute before any analysis: the minimum detectable difference for 43 Brown chains at alpha 0.05 and 80% power, using the observed chain-level variance. If the detectable difference exceeds 0.326, the test is underpowered and the decision stands at do_not_proceed.
design.controls: Adjust for shot distance and result, defender matchup minutes, lineup, season, and playoff status. Use a hierarchical or shrinkage model with initiator as a random effect so small-sample Brown estimates are shrunk toward the teammate mean.
design.falsification: Pre-register a placebo: run the same contrast for each other high-usage teammate with Tatum. If the Brown-specific premium is not larger than the placebo distribution, the premium is not initiator-specific.
design.multiplicity: Test one pre-specified contrast (Brown versus pooled teammates). Report all other initiator and play-type contrasts as exploratory with multiplicity correction.
design.decision_rule: Conclude 'supported' only if the adjusted Brown-minus-teammate difference exceeds the placebo distribution and its confidence interval excludes zero, with the lower bound above a pre-registered minimum effect. Conclude 'rejected' if the CI is narrow enough to exclude 0.326 and the premium is not separated from the baseline. Otherwise conclude 'uncertain'.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-06-14: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded as partial.

methodological_questions: Is the Brown-specific PNR premium distinguishable from any-teammate DRIVE-to-Tatum PNR effects given n=43 Brown chains?
What sample size and exposure is needed to test an initiator-specific premium against a teammate baseline?
How reliable and stable are play-type point-value estimates derived from play-by-play?
What confounders (shot quality, defensive matchups, lineup, playoff vs regular season) threaten initiator-specific PNR comparisons?
args.query: Brown->Tatum PNR premium +0.326 initiator-specific versus any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum pick-and-roll points per chain, sample size, derived play-type labels from play-by-play, defensive matchup confounding

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of possession sequences and transitions):
The reported +0.326 Brown->Tatum PNR premium is Brown-specific, not any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=43 brown chains

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
